# Temple Scroll Column 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 16 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**16:1** On the eighth day an assembly shall be for you; all laborious work you shall not do.

**16:2** And you shall bring near a burnt offering, a fire offering of soothing aroma to the LORD:

**16:3** one young bull, one ram, seven lambs, sons of a year, without blemish.

**16:4** Their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.

**16:5** And one male goat for a sin offering, besides the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

**16:6** These you shall make to the LORD at your appointed feasts,

**16:7** besides your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings

**16:8** and for your grain offerings and for your drink offerings and for your peace offerings.

**16:9** vacat

**16:10** And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

**16:11** Command the sons of Israel, saying to them: When you come into the land

**16:12** which I am giving to you for an inheritance, and you dwell in it,

**16:13** and you say, I will set over me a king like all the nations that are round about me —

**16:14** you shall surely set over you a king whom I shall choose.

**16:15** From among your brothers you shall set over you a king;

**16:16** you shall not be able to set over you a foreign man who is not your brother.

**16:17** Only he shall not multiply for himself horses, and he shall not return the people to Egypt

**16:18** in order to multiply horses, since I said to you: You shall not return again by this way.

---

*EMET notes: Column 16 is well preserved. Lines 1-8 complete the Sukkot legislation with the eighth-day assembly (atseret), paralleling Numbers 29:35-39. The reduced offering (one bull, one ram, seven lambs) contrasts with the seven-day sequence. After a vacat (section break), lines 10-18 transition to the Law of the King, paralleling Deuteronomy 17:14-16 — a major shift from cultic legislation to constitutional law. The Temple Scroll's characteristic divine first-person voice continues.*
